newsitem.title: USA: Calif. exports drop 1.2 pct on weak electronics.
newsitem.headline: Calif. exports drop 1.2 pct on weak electronics.

text.p: California exports slipped 1.2 percent in the first quarter to $25.3 billion, reflecting a drop in demand for electronic equipment, according to a state report released on Wednesday.

State exports of electronics -- a category that includes computers and computer parts -- fell 8.1 percent in the quarter. Exports of industrial machinery and transportation equipment also fell in the first quarter, the state's Trade and Commerce Agency said in its preliminary trade report.
California food and agricultural crop exports surged in the first quarter by 10.5 percent and 18.4 percent respectively, according to the report.
California exports of manufactured goods to Mexico rose 16 percent to $2.4 billion in the first quarter, compared to the first quarter of 1996, the Trade and Commerce Agency said.
Exports to China and Hong Kong were up 14 percent and 20 percent respectively. Combined exports to China and Hong Kong would make them California's fifth largest export market.
Exports to Japan, Korea, Singapore and Malaysia dropped in the first quarter, according to the report.
